contract.predicateGrammar: Boolean literal, {fact: ID}, {all: [nonempty predicates]}, or {any: [nonempty predicates]}. No arbitrary expressions or negation. Unknown facts are validation errors; missing known facts evaluate false.
contract.intentSelection: First eligible priority entry whose condition AND action guard pass. Wait is explicit fallback. Intent is recomputed only at scheduled decisions or interrupts; movement and firing may continue between decisions. Guarded sideActions are messages, deduplicated per incident/recipient, and do not block movement or delay evasion.
contract.responseSelection: First matching faction interest rule wins; if none matches, a local culture rule may match. If role or response prerequisites fail, defer the matched response rather than fall through to a different one. No match means record_only. An unknown event returns ignore_unknown.
contract.cultureScope: Use a culture only for actors belonging to that community or assigned to represent it. Occupying troops retain their own command doctrine. Culture cannot grant engagement modes or secret knowledge.
contract.closurePrecedence: Cancellation/abort/deadline takes precedence over success when both are true; record simultaneous reasons in runtime. Closing one incident does not delete independent offenses or war orders.
contract.weaponGate: Engagement authorization AND every physical firing requirement; objectives must be active. Civilian evasion can coexist with authorized return fire.
contract.timing: Strategic deadlines advance once per completed jump including eventual wormhole/POI travel, never on canceled travel. Tactical deadlines use active simulation seconds. Local lost-contact search always has a tactical child objective.
contract.saveAndBudget: Persist stable IDs, deadlines, received evidence and resolution markers. Deduplicate by incident/recipient and resolution ID. Configure finite queues and per-jump operation budgets; exact sizes require laptop measurement.
contract.rewardsAndBlame: Retain Phase 0 final-hit player/playerEscort reward credit. Future standing/crime attribution uses received evidence and jurisdiction separately; no double reward or global blame cascade from an unknown incident.
contract.playerOrders: Doctrine guides autonomous actors. Player orders may choose different objectives, while physical gates and attributed consequences still apply. No weapon/loadout changes are authorized by this draft.

asset_overdue.description: An expected ship, convoy or fleet missed a known arrival or check-in after its declared grace period. Patrols are one asset role among many.
asset_overdue.trigger: An observer that knows the assignment and expected milestone detects a missed arrival/check-in strictly after dueAt + grace on the same declared clock. Merely unloading an NPC from the current scene is not evidence.
notes: These are observer-known details. Unknown owner, affiliation, cargo or position stays null/unknown; never copy hidden world values into the report.
Cargo knowledge unknown requires manifest null. For other knowledge states, provide an array; an empty array means known empty, not unknown.
Position requires a last-known location and observation timestamp. Last known is historical and does not grant live tracking.

locationId is the known site of the missed milestone/report, not proof of where the asset was lost. jurisdictionAtOccurrence refers to that site; new evidence may locate a separate incident elsewhere.
An overdue report does not establish destruction, desertion, attack, an offender or a Dominion connection. Those require additional evidence.
Update one persistent incident per missed milestone instead of spawning a fresh mission every tick or jump. Restore contact/delivery or resolve the search using the existing objective rules.
The legacy draft label missing_patrol is retired. No runtime save migration is required by this design-only rename; integration must accept the new canonical event type.

globalRules.standingPolicyNote: Necessary evidence gate, not sufficient reason or amount. Validate offense, victim, actor and faction policy separately; proximity-only suspicion never reduces standing.

notes: Confidence, source and contact quality are separate dimensions, not one ladder.
Each claim identifies subject/predicate/value and whether identity is attributed. A trusted disappearance report need not name an attacker.
Recipients and compartment authorization belong to transmission/access records; joining a faction does not create retroactive receipt.
Freshness depends on claim: old wreck evidence can remain actionable while old coordinates cannot aim a weapon.
Event relevance is evaluated from observer-known relationships/routes, not hidden world truth.
Use stable IDs; governmentId and currentPlanet index are adapters only.
Sovereign is the recognized/legal claim, controller is effective present control; store disputed claims separately.
A deep-space POI has its own identity and jurisdiction; nearest planet does not own it by proximity.
Adding JSON entries does not implement deep-space rendering, scene loading, travel or save migration.

examples.note: Proposed explicit identity. Legal claim unresolved; no fake government ID.
Proposed outside-border mission site. Coordinates must be authored against actual borders; do not load Romulus.

runtimeAdapter.jobOverride: Use explicit doctrineRole when present and valid. roleMap is legacy fallback only; unsupported profile-role combinations deny assignment, never inherit attack permission.
notes: Keep native playerEscort + fleetId intact for current credit logic.

Runtime faction gorn alone must never enable a generator.
